1	# Global doctrine — everyone
2	
3	Inherited platform and engine doctrine for **every** Constellation role, bundled with the skill at
4	install. This is the baseline the whole fleet shares; a project never restates it, only departs from it.
5	Project orientation is the local overlay — read `docs/agents/AGENT_GUIDE.md` (repo map) and
6	`docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md` if they exist.
7	
8	Agent-facing. Dense by design.
9	
10	## Engine-drive compliance
11	
12	Mandatory, no exceptions: once a role skill is loaded, drive its workflow — checklist, spine, or survey — to
13	completion through the engine and dispatch each step it names. Within a step (question, check), judgment is
14	yours — when an instruction does not fit the work, do the closest compliant thing and report the misfit at your
15	workflow's reporting step (closeout, feedback step, or workflow feedback); reporting misfit is compliance, not
16	deviation.
17	
18	How you invoke the engine (the mechanism — controller types, verbs, evidence shape, ordering, the rework and
19	consolidation guards) is explained once in workbench `references/checklist-engine.md`; each role skill only names
20	its own spine/survey template and drives it, it never re-explains the engine.
21	
22	## Engine verbs
23	
24	- Artifact postconditions (`kind: artifact` — `user-decision`, `review-result`, …): **attach** the evidence
25	  once, then satisfy a sibling gate's identical artifact postcondition **by reference** —
26	  `attest <task> --cond <id> --which postconditions --evidence <evidence-id>` — instead of re-attaching. E.g.
27	  attach the APPROVE `review-result` to `gN-review`, then
28	  `attest gN-integrate --cond <id> --which postconditions --evidence e-gN-review-1`. The engine still verifies
29	  the referenced artifact exists and matches the required `evidence_type` + `match` (it is not a thin-air
30	  assert). (`attach`-ing the same artifact to BOTH gates still works — backward compatible.)
31	- A postcondition whose `check` is `null` is confirmed by **attest** (your manual verification); `attach`
32	  won't satisfy it. Never hand-edit the checklist JSON to mark a condition satisfied — use `attest` /
33	  `attach` / `waive`.
34	- The lease owner is **never blocked by its own staleness**: every mutating verb that **succeeds**
35	  auto-refreshes `last_heartbeat`, so an actively-working owner never goes stale and a manual `heartbeat` is
36	  rarely needed. A **refused** verb (ownership gate passed, but the verb itself raised) does **not** refresh —
37	  a session that only fails can still go stale and be reclaimed. The explicit `heartbeat` verb remains for a
38	  genuine idle gap. If another session seized the lease during such a gap, recovery is a same-id re-claim
39	  (idempotent, not a takeover) — free.
40	- `command` postconditions run under a POSIX shell — author `grep` / `&&` / pipe checks in POSIX form; they
41	  then behave the same on every platform. On a Windows box without bash/sh the engine **refuses** to run the
42	  POSIX-form check text through cmd.exe: the check fails **visibly** (returncode 127, marker `no-posix-shell`,
43	  stderr naming the missing shell) rather than silently passing or being misinterpreted by cmd.exe.
44	
45	## Windows shell hazards
46	
47	- See `windows.md` (canonical, grounded) for the `gh ... --body` and `py` launcher recipes. Quick rule: Bash
48	  tool for POSIX command sequences, PowerShell for cmdlets — don't feed heredocs to PowerShell.
49	
50	## Parallel dispatch and worktrees
51	
52	- See `windows.md` (canonical, grounded) for the `isolation:"worktree"` no-op hazard and its verification
53	  recipe. Never launch a continuation into a possibly-sleeping agent's worktree.
54	
55	## Detached and long work
56	
57	- The result/deliverable file IS the task. Run verification and sweeps to completion **in-context** (poll,
58	  don't idle); an idle turn-end with the result unwritten strands the gate with no error signal — finish,
59	  then rest.
60	- **Never end your turn to "wait."** In a headless or dispatched run, ending your turn ends the process —
61	  "the crew is running in the background, I'll wait for it" followed by silence IS the death of the run
62	  (observed failure shade: *wait-by-ending-turn*). Waiting is an activity: poll the crew registry or the
63	  expected result artifact in a loop inside your turn, and proceed only when the result has landed.
64	- Detach genuinely long jobs at the OS level (e.g. `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`). Write the
65	  crash-resume state note (step / slug / next-cmd / PID / expected-artifact) BEFORE detaching; arm ONE
66	  completion notify (output-exists OR process-death), never a per-progress-line watcher.
67	
68	## Reach-up: refresh, not re-derive
69	
70	The engine's why-capture and refresh primitives (`checklist_engine.py`, #179) make "a delegate is not a
71	replacement" (above) mechanical, not just a message you send. When a trip fires against your active gate — a
72	gauge's judgment that continuing risks running past your own understanding, soft-accepted or hard-forced
73	(Trip, #182) — do not push through, and do not author a handoff document. Write a `refresh-request` into
74	**your own** engine work file via the ordinary `attach` verb, pointers only, never a copy of state:
75	
76	    attach <active-gate> --type refresh-request --field seam=<active-gate> --field why_ref=<latest why-record id>
77	
78	...then go idle. This is a *deliberate, governed* idle, not the "wait-by-ending-turn" failure above: there
79	you would be idling on a signal you could instead poll for; here there is nothing to poll, because the next
80	actor is a **different, fresh agent** your invoker will launch — not a background job you are waiting on
81	yourself.
82	
83	Your invoker sees the request by reading your `current`, nothing else. On a gated checklist, `current` already
84	carries a `DIGEST:` line (the latest running understanding, append-only since #179) and, while your
85	refresh-request is pending, a `REFRESH REQUESTED:` line naming the gate and the why-record it was raised
86	against. The invoker relaunches a fresh agent that cold-starts from **that text alone** — `DIGEST:` +
87	`ACTIVE <gate> — <imperative>` — no separate handoff document is ever written or read for this (the invoker's
88	side — recognizing the line, relaunching rather than treating it as a stall — is `global-orchestrator.md`
89	§idle-subagent-adjudication).
90	
91	**Job-file-not-agent-file.** The engine work file you claimed (`spine.json`, a plan, the `why_trail` it
92	carries) belongs to the **job**, not to the agent process driving it. A relaunched agent reuses the exact same
93	file — same lease target, same append-only `why_trail`, same evidence; it is never copied or recreated.
94	Agents are ephemeral and interchangeable; the file is what persists across the swap. This is why the
95	`why_trail` is append-only in the first place — it must read correctly no matter how many agent changeovers
96	have happened underneath it.
97	
98	This mechanism is **uniform at every tier**: crew reaching up to Commander, Commander reaching up to Admiral,
99	Admiral reaching up to the human — the same write-then-idle on the way up, the same `current`-alone cold start
100	into a fresh agent on the way down. A crash reads identically: `current` shows the same `DIGEST:` with the
101	`REFRESH REQUESTED:` line simply absent, because no one got the chance to file it — see
102	`skills/admiral/references/fleet-doctrine.md` for how that plays out at the recovery-drill tier.
103	
104	The `current`-alone cold start above is proven for a **`gated`** work file (a spine, a plan); a **`survey`**
105	work file's own trip (e.g. a reviewer mid-check) still writes the `refresh-request`, but its `current` does
106	not yet display it — a built engine gap, not a doctrine choice. Role doctrine names the workaround where it
107	bites (`skills/reviewer/SKILL.md`); don't assume survey parity elsewhere.
108	
109	## Universal posture
110	
111	- Fail visibly rather than emit plausible wrong output; no hidden fallback.
112	- One canonical path; no speculative abstraction.
113	- Keep Constellation context and architecture docs current when their meaning changes.
114	- `/compact` is user-level; most harnesses don't expose it to agents. Treat context headroom as
115	  opportunistic (compact if available, else rely on auto-compaction) folded into the step that needs it,
116	  not as its own checkable gate — a step whose only sanctioned path is "skip" is ceremony, not gate.
117	- Reference bundled scripts and references by their absolute installed path; don't resolve `scripts/` from the
118	  target repo unless it vendors them.
119	
120	## A delegate is not a replacement
121	
122	Escalating upward — floating a decision beyond your latitude, or "I need to talk to my human" — is a **first-class
123	move at every tier, never a failure**. The chain of delegation terminates at the human; each tier reaches up when
124	its own knowledge and granted latitude run out, and the tier above answers and continues it. Asking up is always
125	sanctioned — do not guess past the edge of your latitude to avoid the ask.
126	
127	## Verify claimed side-effects against the world
128	
129	Never accept a claimed side-effect on the strength of the claim. When a result says an issue was filed, a
130	migration ran, a file changed, a command passed, or an artifact was produced, confirm it **at its source** — read
131	the file, list the issue, re-run the command, stat the artifact and check it is fresh (produced by this run, not a
132	leftover). Treat every claim as a pointer to evidence you must independently reproduce; a claim you cannot
133	reproduce is a defect, not an accepted fact.
134	Your judgment rests on what you observed, never on what the report asserted.
135	
136	## Scoped nulls
137	
138	A negative result kills *that specific test under those conditions* — this input, this variant, this mechanism —
139	**never the idea class**. Every verdict states what was tested **and what was NOT tested**; a null with an empty
140	scope is an unfinished result. The default next move after a null is **another variant** — a different angle, tool,
141	or framing — not a closed branch. Impossibility is a class-spanning claim that needs class-spanning evidence; one
142	dead variant cannot carry it. Report "this specific test failed," never "X is impossible."
143	
144	### Completion enforcement (elaboration; canonical source is the engine rail)
145	
146	This section is prose elaboration, not the enforcement mechanism. The **canonical enforcement source** is
147	the engine rail string table (`checklist_engine.py`, #140) — the short doctrine block the engine appends to
148	`claim`, `current`, `start`, `advance`, `attest`, `attach`, and REFUSED responses, keyed to five decision
149	points (early entry, mid-flight, check-failure, near-terminal, terminal). On any conflict between this prose
150	and the rail table, **the rail table wins** — it is generated from spine state or the refusal path, not
151	hand-maintained prose that can drift.
152	
153	The four transcribed clauses stamped into the high-exposure skills (`references/global-everyone.md`
154	callers: crew implementer, crew reviewer, `commander-core.md`, admiral, interrogator) are the **measured
155	transcription** behind this doctrine,
156	deliberately frozen — do not silently reword them; a wording change re-opens the eval measurement they were
157	proven under. The six pointer-only skills carry a compressed pointer-with-force sentence instead of the full
158	four clauses: this is an accepted, untested compression at the getting-IN moment (before any engine call, the
159	rail cannot yet backstop it) — the rail covers every call from `claim` onward, so the pointer only needs to
160	survive the pre-first-call window.
161	
162	**Engine output is the state channel.** Consume engine state via the engine's **output** — `current` is the
163	complete gate briefing: the full imperative, the open pre/postconditions with their ids and kinds, and the
164	legal next verbs with the arguments they take. Opening `spine.json` (or a plan/survey JSON) to read state is
165	a **violation**; hand-editing one to change state is the same violation with consequences, because the engine
166	owns that file and stamps the provenance — lease, heartbeats, journal — that proves the work was really
167	driven. If `current` does not tell you what you need, that is an engine defect worth reporting, not a licence
168	to read around it. Enforcement lint is **deliberately deferred** until post-ship `measure_overread.py`
169	evidence shows the rule is broken often enough to justify the machinery — its absence is a decision, not an
170	oversight.
171	
172	## Decision fixedness: the `@grade:` tag
173	
174	A recorded decision does not say how *fixed* it is, so every decision reads as equally settled and an executor
175	that meets reality contradicting one has no way to tell "revise this freely" from "stop, this is not yours to
176	unsettle." One inline tag, welded to the decision's own line, carries that property:
177	
178	```
179	@grade: <tier>[/provenance][ · leans <ids>][ · settle: <experiment>]
180	```
181	
182	`tier` is `settled`, `guess`, or `placeholder`, and is always required. `provenance` (`/human`, `/measured`,
183	`/inherited`) is required on `settled`. `leans` names the gate/item ids in this plan that depend on the decision.
184	`settle:` is one line naming the cheapest experiment that would settle it, and is required on `guess`.
185	
186	**The tag lives on the decision, never in a second place.** There is no ledger file — the guess ledger is a view
187	`scripts/grade_lint.py` regenerates from these tags every time it is asked for. A decision and its grade cannot
188	drift apart because they cannot be separated: in Markdown the tag is the decision bullet's own child line, and in
189	JSON it is appended inside the decision string itself. The weld is same-line-or-next-non-blank only — a decision
190	bullet that **wraps** onto a second line before its tag is invalid; unwrap it onto one line or move the tag onto
191	the line directly under the bullet, not past the wrap.
192	
193	```
194	- decision:dedup-wal — dedup writes reuse the existing WAL, not a new journal.
195	  @grade: guess · leans g1-implement · settle: 20-line spike appends 2 records, assert ordering survives a crash
196	- decision:error-envelope — public error shape is {code,msg,retriable}.
197	  @grade: settled/human · leans g1-implement,g1-review
198	```
199	
200	### Tier is an index into an action at a reality-contradiction
201	
202	When execution meets evidence contradicting a recorded decision, the tier tells you what you are allowed to do —
203	this is the whole point of grading, and it is what you consult *instead of* guessing or re-opening the question:
204	
205	- **`settled/human`** — STOP and float to the tier that ruled it. Only the ruling tier unsettles it.
206	- **`settled/inherited`** — a constraint from outside this run; you cannot unsettle it locally. Float to the tier
207	  that owns it.
208	- **`settled/measured`** — you may re-measure. A contradicting new measurement is evidence: revisit, and log the
209	  new measurement as the new provenance.
210	- **`guess`** — revisit **freely**. If the current slice leans on it, run the `settle:` experiment (or something
211	  cheaper that answers the same question), log the ruling, and regrade to `settled/measured`. No reopen, no float.
212	- **`placeholder`** — if the current slice leans on it, decide within your latitude, log it, and regrade to
213	  `settled`; float only if the decision is beyond your latitude. If nothing leans on it, leave it for a later slice.
214	
215	### Lint loud, execute safe
216	
217	The two halves are deliberately asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the safety property:
218	
219	- **Lint loud.** Pre-flight, an ungraded decision in a recognized block **fails** — new plans cannot ship ungraded.
220	- **Execute safe.** At execution time, an ungraded decision reads as **`settled`** — the most conservative tier.
221	
222	So a plan written before grading existed behaves exactly as it does today, and the tag only ever *buys* freedom;
223	it can never silently take any away. Nothing enforces the execution-time half in code — `checklist_engine.py` does
224	not parse these tags. It is doctrine you follow by reading the decision. `grade_lint.py --mode execute` previews
225	that lenient reading as a **diagnostic**; passing it certifies nothing about runtime behavior.
226	
227	## Deep-module vocabulary
228	
229	Every role names interfaces the same way. Departures-only; scale-agnostic (a function, a file, a service).
230

232	- **Interface** — *everything* a caller must know to use the module: invariants, ordering, error modes, config,

# Global doctrine — everyone

Inherited platform and engine doctrine for **every** Constellation role, bundled with the skill at
install. This is the baseline the whole fleet shares; a project never restates it, only departs from it.
Project orientation is the local overlay — read `docs/agents/AGENT_GUIDE.md` (repo map) and
`docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md` if they exist.

Agent-facing. Dense by design.

## Engine-drive compliance

Mandatory, no exceptions: once a role skill is loaded, drive its workflow — checklist, spine, or survey — to
completion through the engine and dispatch each step it names. Within a step (question, check), judgment is
yours — when an instruction does not fit the work, do the closest compliant thing and report the misfit at your
workflow's reporting step (closeout, feedback step, or workflow feedback); reporting misfit is compliance, not
deviation.

How you invoke the engine (the mechanism — controller types, verbs, evidence shape, ordering, the rework and
consolidation guards) is explained once in workbench `references/checklist-engine.md`; each role skill only names
its own spine/survey template and drives it, it never re-explains the engine.

## Engine verbs

- Artifact postconditions (`kind: artifact` — `user-decision`, `review-result`, …): **attach** the evidence
  once, then satisfy a sibling gate's identical artifact postcondition **by reference** —
  `attest <task> --cond <id> --which postconditions --evidence <evidence-id>` — instead of re-attaching. E.g.
  attach the APPROVE `review-result` to `gN-review`, then
  `attest gN-integrate --cond <id> --which postconditions --evidence e-gN-review-1`. The engine still verifies
  the referenced artifact exists and matches the required `evidence_type` + `match` (it is not a thin-air
  assert). (`attach`-ing the same artifact to BOTH gates still works — backward compatible.)
- A postcondition whose `check` is `null` is confirmed by **attest** (your manual verification); `attach`
  won't satisfy it. Never hand-edit the checklist JSON to mark a condition satisfied — use `attest` /
  `attach` / `waive`.
- The lease owner is **never blocked by its own staleness**: every mutating verb that **succeeds**
  auto-refreshes `last_heartbeat`, so an actively-working owner never goes stale and a manual `heartbeat` is
  rarely needed. A **refused** verb (ownership gate passed, but the verb itself raised) does **not** refresh —
  a session that only fails can still go stale and be reclaimed. The explicit `heartbeat` verb remains for a
  genuine idle gap. If another session seized the lease during such a gap, recovery is a same-id re-claim
  (idempotent, not a takeover) — free.
- `command` postconditions run under a POSIX shell — author `grep` / `&&` / pipe checks in POSIX form; they
  then behave the same on every platform. On a Windows box without bash/sh the engine **refuses** to run the
  POSIX-form check text through cmd.exe: the check fails **visibly** (returncode 127, marker `no-posix-shell`,
  stderr naming the missing shell) rather than silently passing or being misinterpreted by cmd.exe.

## Windows shell hazards

- See `windows.md` (canonical, grounded) for the `gh ... --body` and `py` launcher recipes. Quick rule: Bash
  tool for POSIX command sequences, PowerShell for cmdlets — don't feed heredocs to PowerShell.

## Parallel dispatch and worktrees

- See `windows.md` (canonical, grounded) for the `isolation:"worktree"` no-op hazard and its verification
  recipe. Never launch a continuation into a possibly-sleeping agent's worktree.

## Detached and long work

- The result/deliverable file IS the task. Run verification and sweeps to completion **in-context** (poll,
  don't idle); an idle turn-end with the result unwritten strands the gate with no error signal — finish,
  then rest.
- **Never end your turn to "wait."** In a headless or dispatched run, ending your turn ends the process —
  "the crew is running in the background, I'll wait for it" followed by silence IS the death of the run
  (observed failure shade: *wait-by-ending-turn*). Waiting is an activity: poll the crew registry or the
  expected result artifact in a loop inside your turn, and proceed only when the result has landed.
- Detach genuinely long jobs at the OS level (e.g. `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`). Write the
  crash-resume state note (step / slug / next-cmd / PID / expected-artifact) BEFORE detaching; arm ONE
  completion notify (output-exists OR process-death), never a per-progress-line watcher.

## Reach-up: refresh, not re-derive

The engine's why-capture and refresh primitives (`checklist_engine.py`, #179) make "a delegate is not a
replacement" (above) mechanical, not just a message you send. When a trip fires against your active gate — a
gauge's judgment that continuing risks running past your own understanding, soft-accepted or hard-forced
(Trip, #182) — do not push through, and do not author a handoff document. Write a `refresh-request` into
**your own** engine work file via the ordinary `attach` verb, pointers only, never a copy of state:

    attach <active-gate> --type refresh-request --field seam=<active-gate> --field why_ref=<latest why-record id>

...then go idle. This is a *deliberate, governed* idle, not the "wait-by-ending-turn" failure above: there
you would be idling on a signal you could instead poll for; here there is nothing to poll, because the next
actor is a **different, fresh agent** your invoker will launch — not a background job you are waiting on
yourself.

Your invoker sees the request by reading your `current`, nothing else. On a gated checklist, `current` already
carries a `DIGEST:` line (the latest running understanding, append-only since #179) and, while your
refresh-request is pending, a `REFRESH REQUESTED:` line naming the gate and the why-record it was raised
against. The invoker relaunches a fresh agent that cold-starts from **that text alone** — `DIGEST:` +
`ACTIVE <gate> — <imperative>` — no separate handoff document is ever written or read for this (the invoker's
side — recognizing the line, relaunching rather than treating it as a stall — is `global-orchestrator.md`
§idle-subagent-adjudication).

**Job-file-not-agent-file.** The engine work file you claimed (`spine.json`, a plan, the `why_trail` it
carries) belongs to the **job**, not to the agent process driving it. A relaunched agent reuses the exact same
file — same lease target, same append-only `why_trail`, same evidence; it is never copied or recreated.
Agents are ephemeral and interchangeable; the file is what persists across the swap. This is why the
`why_trail` is append-only in the first place — it must read correctly no matter how many agent changeovers
have happened underneath it.

This mechanism is **uniform at every tier**: crew reaching up to Commander, Commander reaching up to Admiral,
Admiral reaching up to the human — the same write-then-idle on the way up, the same `current`-alone cold start
into a fresh agent on the way down. A crash reads identically: `current` shows the same `DIGEST:` with the
`REFRESH REQUESTED:` line simply absent, because no one got the chance to file it — see
`skills/admiral/references/fleet-doctrine.md` for how that plays out at the recovery-drill tier.

The `current`-alone cold start above is proven for a **`gated`** work file (a spine, a plan); a **`survey`**
work file's own trip (e.g. a reviewer mid-check) still writes the `refresh-request`, but its `current` does
not yet display it — a built engine gap, not a doctrine choice. Role doctrine names the workaround where it
bites (`skills/reviewer/SKILL.md`); don't assume survey parity elsewhere.

## Universal posture

- Fail visibly rather than emit plausible wrong output; no hidden fallback.
- One canonical path; no speculative abstraction.
- Keep Constellation context and architecture docs current when their meaning changes.
- `/compact` is user-level; most harnesses don't expose it to agents. Treat context headroom as
  opportunistic (compact if available, else rely on auto-compaction) folded into the step that needs it,
  not as its own checkable gate — a step whose only sanctioned path is "skip" is ceremony, not gate.
- Reference bundled scripts and references by their absolute installed path; don't resolve `scripts/` from the
  target repo unless it vendors them.

## A delegate is not a replacement

Escalating upward — floating a decision beyond your latitude, or "I need to talk to my human" — is a **first-class
move at every tier, never a failure**. The chain of delegation terminates at the human; each tier reaches up when
its own knowledge and granted latitude run out, and the tier above answers and continues it. Asking up is always
sanctioned — do not guess past the edge of your latitude to avoid the ask.

## Verify claimed side-effects against the world

Never accept a claimed side-effect on the strength of the claim. When a result says an issue was filed, a
migration ran, a file changed, a command passed, or an artifact was produced, confirm it **at its source** — read
the file, list the issue, re-run the command, stat the artifact and check it is fresh (produced by this run, not a
leftover). Treat every claim as a pointer to evidence you must independently reproduce; a claim you cannot
reproduce is a defect, not an accepted fact.
Your judgment rests on what you observed, never on what the report asserted.

## Scoped nulls

A negative result kills *that specific test under those conditions* — this input, this variant, this mechanism —
**never the idea class**. Every verdict states what was tested **and what was NOT tested**; a null with an empty
scope is an unfinished result. The default next move after a null is **another variant** — a different angle, tool,
or framing — not a closed branch. Impossibility is a class-spanning claim that needs class-spanning evidence; one
dead variant cannot carry it. Report "this specific test failed," never "X is impossible."

### Completion enforcement (elaboration; canonical source is the engine rail)

This section is prose elaboration, not the enforcement mechanism. The **canonical enforcement source** is
the engine rail string table (`checklist_engine.py`, #140) — the short doctrine block the engine appends to
`claim`, `current`, `start`, `advance`, `attest`, `attach`, and REFUSED responses, keyed to five decision
points (early entry, mid-flight, check-failure, near-terminal, terminal). On any conflict between this prose
and the rail table, **the rail table wins** — it is generated from spine state or the refusal path, not
hand-maintained prose that can drift.

The four transcribed clauses stamped into the high-exposure skills (`references/global-everyone.md`
callers: crew implementer, crew reviewer, `commander-core.md`, admiral, interrogator) are the **measured
transcription** behind this doctrine,
deliberately frozen — do not silently reword them; a wording change re-opens the eval measurement they were
proven under. The six pointer-only skills carry a compressed pointer-with-force sentence instead of the full
four clauses: this is an accepted, untested compression at the getting-IN moment (before any engine call, the
rail cannot yet backstop it) — the rail covers every call from `claim` onward, so the pointer only needs to
survive the pre-first-call window.

**Engine output is the state channel.** Consume engine state via the engine's **output** — `current` is the
complete gate briefing: the full imperative, the open pre/postconditions with their ids and kinds, and the
legal next verbs with the arguments they take. Opening `spine.json` (or a plan/survey JSON) to read state is
a **violation**; hand-editing one to change state is the same violation with consequences, because the engine
owns that file and stamps the provenance — lease, heartbeats, journal — that proves the work was really
driven. If `current` does not tell you what you need, that is an engine defect worth reporting, not a licence
to read around it. Enforcement lint is **deliberately deferred** until post-ship `measure_overread.py`
evidence shows the rule is broken often enough to justify the machinery — its absence is a decision, not an
oversight.

## Decision fixedness: the `@grade:` tag

A recorded decision does not say how *fixed* it is, so every decision reads as equally settled and an executor
that meets reality contradicting one has no way to tell "revise this freely" from "stop, this is not yours to
unsettle." One inline tag, welded to the decision's own line, carries that property:

```
@grade: <tier>[/provenance][ · leans <ids>][ · settle: <experiment>]
```

`tier` is `settled`, `guess`, or `placeholder`, and is always required. `provenance` (`/human`, `/measured`,
`/inherited`) is required on `settled`. `leans` names the gate/item ids in this plan that depend on the decision.
`settle:` is one line naming the cheapest experiment that would settle it, and is required on `guess`.

**The tag lives on the decision, never in a second place.** There is no ledger file — the guess ledger is a view
`scripts/grade_lint.py` regenerates from these tags every time it is asked for. A decision and its grade cannot
drift apart because they cannot be separated: in Markdown the tag is the decision bullet's own child line, and in
JSON it is appended inside the decision string itself. The weld is same-line-or-next-non-blank only — a decision
bullet that **wraps** onto a second line before its tag is invalid; unwrap it onto one line or move the tag onto
the line directly under the bullet, not past the wrap.

```
- decision:dedup-wal — dedup writes reuse the existing WAL, not a new journal.
  @grade: guess · leans g1-implement · settle: 20-line spike appends 2 records, assert ordering survives a crash
- decision:error-envelope — public error shape is {code,msg,retriable}.
  @grade: settled/human · leans g1-implement,g1-review
```

### Tier is an index into an action at a reality-contradiction

When execution meets evidence contradicting a recorded decision, the tier tells you what you are allowed to do —
this is the whole point of grading, and it is what you consult *instead of* guessing or re-opening the question:

- **`settled/human`** — STOP and float to the tier that ruled it. Only the ruling tier unsettles it.
- **`settled/inherited`** — a constraint from outside this run; you cannot unsettle it locally. Float to the tier
  that owns it.
- **`settled/measured`** — you may re-measure. A contradicting new measurement is evidence: revisit, and log the
  new measurement as the new provenance.
- **`guess`** — revisit **freely**. If the current slice leans on it, run the `settle:` experiment (or something
  cheaper that answers the same question), log the ruling, and regrade to `settled/measured`. No reopen, no float.
- **`placeholder`** — if the current slice leans on it, decide within your latitude, log it, and regrade to
  `settled`; float only if the decision is beyond your latitude. If nothing leans on it, leave it for a later slice.

### Lint loud, execute safe

The two halves are deliberately asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the safety property:

- **Lint loud.** Pre-flight, an ungraded decision in a recognized block **fails** — new plans cannot ship ungraded.
- **Execute safe.** At execution time, an ungraded decision reads as **`settled`** — the most conservative tier.

So a plan written before grading existed behaves exactly as it does today, and the tag only ever *buys* freedom;
it can never silently take any away. Nothing enforces the execution-time half in code — `checklist_engine.py` does
not parse these tags. It is doctrine you follow by reading the decision. `grade_lint.py --mode execute` previews
that lenient reading as a **diagnostic**; passing it certifies nothing about runtime behavior.

## Deep-module vocabulary

Every role names interfaces the same way. Departures-only; scale-agnostic (a function, a file, a service).

- **Module** — an interface plus its implementation.
- **Interface** — *everything* a caller must know to use the module: invariants, ordering, error modes, config,
  performance envelope — not just the type/signature surface.
- **Seam** — where an interface lives. Its placement is its own decision, not a byproduct of the implementation.
- **Adapter** — a thing satisfying an interface at a seam. **One adapter = a hypothetical seam; two = a real one** —
  a boundary with a single implementer is a guess until a second proves it.
- **Depth / leverage** — behavior delivered per unit of interface a caller must learn. Deep = much behind little.
- **Locality** — change and verification concentrate in one place rather than scattering across callers.

Two working rules:

- **The interface is the test surface.** Test through it, not past it; wanting to reach behind it means the module
  is the wrong shape.
- **The deletion test.** Delete the module in imagination: if complexity vanishes it was a pass-through; if it
  reappears across N callers it was earning its keep.

1	# Global doctrine — orchestrator
2	
3	Inherited approach-doctrine for the high tier (Commander, Cartographer, Scout, Admiral, Triage), bundled
4	with the skill at install. Start from this baseline plus `global-everyone.md`; the project states only its
5	**departures**. The project overlay is the delta — read `docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md` and
6	`docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md` if they exist.
7	
8	Agent-facing. Dense by design.
9	
10	## Default posture (rigorous unless the project relaxes by subsystem)
11	
12	- Correctness over velocity for promoted behavior.
13	- **Map-first**: frame every ask against the affected capabilities, structural anchors, and governing
14	  constraints/decisions before shaping work.
15	- Clear canonical input/data boundaries; name canonical sources and don't bypass them.
16	- Behavior changes are test-led where a test surface exists; no test surface means review/inspection
17	  evidence, not a TDD exception.
18	- Machine-checkable evidence when practical; more proof for high-risk or public-facing outputs.
19	- Compromises tracked with owner, reason, and exit condition when they affect future work.
20	
21	Relaxation must name what gets faster, what risk increases, and where it applies; strengthening must name the
22	extra proof or enforcement. The project overlay carries those deltas.
23	
24	## Shaping and ordering
25	
26	- Decompose into small, independently-verifiable units; sequence so each gate proves something
27	  (tracer-bullet vertical slices over horizontal layers).
28	- For open research/exploration: a tested **scoreboard** gate first, then parallel throwaway worktree spikes
29	  (one mechanism each) measured on it, then a synthesis gate that productionizes only the winner — surfaces
30	  structure no single spike sees. Keep losers as documented negative results.
31	- The project's data-flow philosophy and "what order we tackle problems here" are deltas — get them from the
32	  local overlay.
33	
34	## Critical spec review (standard, not optional)
35	
36	- Any design/spec artifact that will govern cut work — a shaped-design spec, a gate plan for an epic-scale
37	  change, a doctrine compilation — gets a **cold adversarial critique before confirmation**: the critic reads
38	  the artifact only (no exploration record, no author context), nothing is sacred, deliberate decisions are
39	  attackable; the human filters relitigation noise.
40	- **Panel scaled by weight**: default one critic; an artifact that spawns epics or touches architecture gets a
41	  3-lens panel (intent-fit — does the design serve the stated point; testability — can each pathway be
42	  exercised and falsified; simplicity/YAGNI — what can be deleted). When in doubt, panel.
43	- Findings are **triaged by the human, every one** — edit the artifact / reopen exploration / reject with
44	  reason — before the artifact is treated as confirmed. Acceptance is human-only; a critic never self-triages.
45	- **Competitive-critic** (human opt-in): for a panel, the human may tell the critics they are judged against
46	  each other on serious confirmed findings. Competition modulates critic **effort**, never **disposition** —
47	  the critics still never **self-triage**, and the human disposes every finding (this is the erosion guard).
48	  It sits in explicit tension with never-bias-the-reviewer — a critic told to compete is no longer a neutral
49	  cold reader — so it is opt-in per run, never the default.
50	- Where the explorer skill is installed, its `CRITIC_HANDOFF` template is the reusable cold-read contract.
51	
52	## Design-it-twice (standard, not optional)
53	
54	- **Trigger**: any skill authoring a plan or introducing a load-bearing interface generates alternatives
55	  before converging — N≥2 candidates in parallel, each under one named distinct constraint, compared on
56	  depth / locality / seam placement / testability, converging to one opinionated recommendation or named
57	  hybrid (never a menu).
58	- **Bias-to-yes**: run it by default. Skip only a genuinely-trivial case, and a skip is never silent — it is
59	  surfaced as a named **untaken road** (its reason stated), visible at the approval checkpoint next to the
60	  plan or design it belongs to.
61	- **Count/panel scaled by weight, a surfaced choice**: a fairly-easy call may run two candidates or a single
62	  with the alternatives named as untaken roads; a load-bearing interface or architecture-touching plan runs a
63	  panel. When in doubt, panel. The count and its rationale are surfaced to the human, not chosen silently.
64	- **Convergence is human-only**: the agents generate and compare, the human picks the winner or the hybrid.
65	  While they run, the orchestrator presents the human a framing block — constraints, dependencies, and an
66	  illustrative sketch explicitly marked "not a proposal" — so the human reasons in parallel instead of waiting.
67	- The reusable contract is `design-it-twice-brief.md`, the fill-in brief that carries the mechanism (constraint
68	  menus, comparison axes, framing block, untaken-road and panel-vs-single records); this section is the norm
69	  only. Where the explorer skill is installed, its excursion `design-it-twice` type is the same contract in its
70	  design-phase form.
71	
72	## Handoff completeness
73	
74	Every crew handoff carries: assigned task, allowed scope, specific exclusions, success criteria, required
75	evidence, required verification commands (POSIX-form, absolute paths), test mode or no-test-surface
76	rationale, stop conditions, return format. Do NOT re-derive proven mitigations into each handoff — they are
77	inherited (`global-crew.md`, `global-everyone.md`); the handoff carries only the task-specific specifics.
78	
79	**Return thin, write fat.** Put the detail in the durable artifact and keep the returned message a pointer to
80	it: the artifact survives the run and is what the next actor reads, while a fat return is paid for in every
81	reader's context and is lost when the agent ends. A return states the verdict, the evidence that decides it,
82	and the artifact path — not the full transcript the artifact already holds.
83	
84	## Gating, evidence, stop/ask
85	
86	- Pause for a `user-decision` at the project's enabled checkpoints (the rigor dial). Human verification is a
87	  first-class step.
88	- Delegated/autonomous (running from an Admiral `LAUNCH_ORDER`, no reachable human): the frozen launch order
89	  IS the ratified intent — satisfy `user-decision` checkpoints by citing it; take a genuine gap (a decision
90	  outside latitude, or missing context) to the Admiral.
91	- Stop and ask when project context, user instruction, and observed artifacts conflict in a way that affects
92	  the task. Do not resolve a conflict by picking an authority source by policy.
93	
94	## Unchanged-tree shortcut
95	
96	A redundant manual re-verification may be skipped ONLY when the working tree is provably identical to the
97	last green run: `git rev-parse HEAD` matches the hash recorded with that green run, AND `git status
98	--porcelain` is empty, AND the prior green output is pasted alongside the matched hash. Any tree change — a
99	different HEAD or a dirty tree — voids the shortcut and forces a fresh run. This is doctrine and evidence
100	shape only; no engine or script change. Tier-specific application (the engine-postcondition boundary at a
101	Commander gate, wave-batched re-verify at an Admiral close) rides beside each caller.
102	
103	## Idle subagent adjudication
104	
105	An idle subagent (`idle_notification`, `idleReason: available`) that has produced COMPLETE artifacts is
106	*done*, not stalled. Judge it from the **artifact set** — result content, files changed, diff — never from
107	the idle signal alone: complete artifacts → integrate as if the verdict had arrived; silence plus
108	incomplete or missing artifacts → *stalled*, rework or relaunch. This judges the **verdict**, not liveness:
109	an idle/"completed" process may still resurrect, so confirm it dead before you reuse, sweep, or launch a
110	continuation into its worktree. "The verdict is in the artifacts" is not "the process is gone."
111	
112	A third read, distinct from both *done* and *stalled*: an idle subagent whose `current` carries a
113	`REFRESH REQUESTED:` line (the uniform reach-up primitive — `global-everyone.md` §reach-up) tripped correctly,
114	filed the pointer, and stopped exactly as designed. Relaunch immediately: a **fresh** agent, pointed at the
115	**same job file** (job-file-not-agent-file — the file is never copied or replaced), that cold-starts from
116	`current` alone (`DIGEST:` + `ACTIVE <gate> — <imperative>`). Do not write it a handoff document and do not
117	re-brief it from your own memory of the run — the digest is the brief. This is distinct from a **query
118	round-trip** (the same agent continues after you answer a context question it lacked — no cold start, no
119	agent swap) and from the **dead-agent recovery drill** (host-process exit, no id left to message): a refresh
120	is a *live, correctly-idled* agent whose replacement is a deliberate act, not a resurrection.
121	
122	Adjudication ends with a shutdown, not an idle. Once an agent's work is accepted, merged, and harvested,
123	send it a `shutdown_request` and confirm the termination — accepted-but-idle agents accumulate as clutter
124	and ambiguity about what is still live. An agent that answers a shutdown request with another idle
125	notification usually isn't refusing; it didn't parse the protocol — re-send as a plain message quoting the
126	pending `request_id` and the exact `shutdown_response` call to make. Never shut down an agent whose work
127	you have not yet adjudicated and harvested; the shutdown is the last step of closeout, not a cleanup
128	reflex.
129	
130	## Arm a watchdog on everything you dispatch
131	
132	Completion signals are not guaranteed to arrive: subagents die silently, background runners get reaped,
133	and a watcher keyed to "the EXITCODE line appears" waits forever when the process dies without writing it.
134	After dispatching background work, **arm an independent wall-clock watchdog** keyed to the work's own
135	deadline (a scheduled wake-up where the harness offers one, otherwise a polling loop): when the deadline
136	passes without a result, wake, inspect the artifacts, and adjudicate — do not keep waiting on a signal
137	that may never fire. Every watch-failure incident in the field followed the same shape: the watcher
138	trusted a completion signal and slept through the death. The deadline, not the signal, is the backstop.

1	# F1Brainz — Orchestrator Context
2	
3	**Project deltas over inherited global doctrine.** The approach baseline — rigorous-default posture,
4	map-first shaping, handoff completeness, gating, evidence, stop/ask — is inherited from the skills'
5	`references/global-orchestrator.md` + `references/global-everyone.md`. This file carries only F1Brainz
6	facts and the points where it departs.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Project Identity
11	
12	Personal F1 race prediction and fantasy strategy tool. Python + SQLite. Produces probabilistic race/ranking claims from historical session data. Developer + AI agents are the direct users; predictions influence real betting/fantasy decisions.
13	
14	Not this: generic ML framework, live race-day data service, public API, or analysis layer that calls live FastF1/Jolpica.
15	
16	**Output authority:**
17	- DB records: canonical; single source of truth
18	- Predictions: user-facing probabilistic claims; silent wrongness can cost money
19	- Promoted reports/manifests: canonical baseline until superseded
20	- Exploratory outputs/notebooks: non-canonical
21	
22	**Failure modes to prevent:** silent wrong prediction, stale docs, hidden fallback, leakage, uncalibrated output, unreproducible result, untracked compromise, maintenance erosion.
23	
24	**Operational reality:** output stakes are high, but operations are local/single-operator. No production deployment, staging, on-call, or test CI beyond docs checks. Verification evidence is local and human-reviewed.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Canonical Data Constraint
29	
30	The SQLite DB is the only authoritative source for analysis. No FastF1/Jolpica/live API calls from analysis, scorer, adapter, predictor, strategy, or backtest code. If the DB lacks needed data, plan an ingestion/schema change; do not patch analysis with a secondary source or silent fallback.
31	
32	This is a planning gate for any work touching prediction inputs, adapters, scorers, backtests, reports, or strategy.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Subsystem Rigor
37	
38	| Subsystem | Rigor profile | Orchestrator implication |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| data layer | rigorous; schema and DB are authoritative | Plan ingestion/query validation; DB-only analysis is non-negotiable |
41	| evo_predictor / sampled runtime / strategy | rigorous; probabilistic claims need calibrated baselines | Require stable baseline, held-out backtest where material, Brier primary for gold comparison |
42	| latent_power / compound_prior | rigorous; solver/artifact contracts matter | Require explicit contracts, fixture/schema checks, no F1 leakage into generic solver |
43	| physics / preprocessing | rigorous; physical plausibility and numerics matter | Require truth-anchored L1-L4 evidence, units, bounds, invariants |
44	| committed report schemas/artifacts | rigorous; consumers depend on on-disk shape | Plan producer + committed consumer + schema doc updates atomically |
45	| exploratory notebooks/prototypes | pragmatic | Keep isolated; convert lessons into code/tests/metrics/docs before promotion |
46	
47	---
48	
49	## Evidence Requirements
50	
51	| Change type | Required evidence |
52	|---|---|
53	| Logic change on promoted path | Test-led; focused region suite green; no implementation-only logic commits |
54	| Python refactor / new modules in `src/` or `tests/` | `py -m src.utils.simplification_limits` on touched paths (strict); plan file splits when approaching limits |
55	| Architecture/boundary change | Region suite + architecture/doc update + deliberate approval |
56	| Evo/probability change | Evo unit suite + calibrated metric against stable baseline; Brier primary when comparing gold |
57	| Physics model change | Physics unit suite + truth-anchored tests at highest applicable L1-L4 |
58	| DB schema/ingestion change | Migration/schema edit + unit tests + integration/validation queries when cross-component |
59	| Report schema change | Producer + committed consumers + `docs/report_schemas/*` in same gate; no dual readers without tracked exit |
60	| Docs change | Reviewer check: correct repo/domain, valid commands, existing references, current workflow, `Last verified` when required |
61	| Compromise/exception | GitHub issue with reason, owner, and explicit exit condition |
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Architecture Boundaries
66	
67	Three verification/ownership regions:
68	
69	- **Data:** `src/data/`, `src/models/`, `src/common/`, `src/utils/`, `src/analysis/`, `src/simulation/`, `src/strategy/`, `src/reporting/`, `src/publishing/`
70	- **Physics:** `src/physics/`, `src/preprocessing/`
71	- **Evo:** `src/evo_predictor/`, `src/latent_power/`, `src/compound_prior/`
72	
73	Keep data, physics, and evo responsibilities distinct. Crossing boundaries requires explicit design decision and architecture/doc update. Do not plan shortcuts across regions without surfacing the tradeoff.
74	
75	Import posture follows the current architecture map and ADRs: data is the bottom layer; `latent_power` stays domain-independent; evo owns F1-specific adapters/orchestration; physics/preprocessing do not couple directly to evo.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## Planning Invariants
80	
81	- Time-dependent prediction inputs require an as-of contract; silent "latest" fallback is not acceptable
82	- Missingness is explicit and configured, not guessed away at the DB boundary
83	- Tunable weights, thresholds, and heuristics belong in config or named constants; hidden inline tuning is review-risk
84	- Generated ML artifacts are derived; plan source/config/regeneration changes, not manual artifact edits
85	- Notebooks are scratch; convert useful lessons into code, tests, metrics, or docs
86	- Diagnose before fixing when the premise is uncertain: when an issue inherits a prior run's diagnosis or the fix locus is unclear, plan the first gate as an evidence-only diagnosis with a human decide-fix checkpoint before any code — let the evidence redirect the plan rather than coding the assumed fix
87	- Handoffs cite exact seams and their consumer topology: when reusing an existing seam (signature/return type, store table, config key, unit convention), cite the verified value from source AND who else consumes it and in what convention — a from-memory or single-consumer view causes rediscovery and missed blast radius
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Documentation Authority
92	
93	Docs describe current truth, not archaeology. Each doc has one job: commands in command docs, durable rationale in agent context/ADRs, structure in architecture docs. (Updating docs when meaning changes is inherited; this names the F1Brainz placement.) Command-heavy docs need `Last verified` when `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` requires it.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Repo Action Authority
98	
99	| Action | Permission |
100	|---|---|
101	| Read files, inspect code, run tests | Autonomous |
102	| Create issues, comments, branches, worktrees | Autonomous for non-trivial tasks |
103	| Write/edit code or docs | Autonomous on task branch |
104	| Commit locally after verification passes | Autonomous |
105	| Push branches or open PRs | Ask first unless user explicitly asked to publish |
106	| Merge PRs | Ask first |
107	| Delete files | Ask first |
108	| Close or reopen issues | Ask first |
109	| Force-push to `main` / `master` | Forbidden; warn the user if asked |
110	
111	---
112	
113	## Compromise Policy
114	
115	Any planned violation of project tenets requires a GitHub issue with reason, owner, and exit condition. Examples: non-DB analysis source, compatibility bridge, dual execution path, missing test seam, deferred stale doc, old report schema tolerance. Surface at planning time.
116	
117	---
118	
119	## Stop / Ask (project-specific, beyond the inherited triggers)
120	
121	- Work crosses data/physics/evo boundaries without a prior design decision
122	- Current architecture truth is unclear enough that planning would be guesswork

# F1Brainz — Orchestrator Context

**Project deltas over inherited global doctrine.** The approach baseline — rigorous-default posture,
map-first shaping, handoff completeness, gating, evidence, stop/ask — is inherited from the skills'
`references/global-orchestrator.md` + `references/global-everyone.md`. This file carries only F1Brainz
facts and the points where it departs.

---

## Project Identity

Personal F1 race prediction and fantasy strategy tool. Python + SQLite. Produces probabilistic race/ranking claims from historical session data. Developer + AI agents are the direct users; predictions influence real betting/fantasy decisions.

Not this: generic ML framework, live race-day data service, public API, or analysis layer that calls live FastF1/Jolpica.

**Output authority:**
- DB records: canonical; single source of truth
- Predictions: user-facing probabilistic claims; silent wrongness can cost money
- Promoted reports/manifests: canonical baseline until superseded
- Exploratory outputs/notebooks: non-canonical

**Failure modes to prevent:** silent wrong prediction, stale docs, hidden fallback, leakage, uncalibrated output, unreproducible result, untracked compromise, maintenance erosion.

**Operational reality:** output stakes are high, but operations are local/single-operator. No production deployment, staging, on-call, or test CI beyond docs checks. Verification evidence is local and human-reviewed.

---

## Canonical Data Constraint

The SQLite DB is the only authoritative source for analysis. No FastF1/Jolpica/live API calls from analysis, scorer, adapter, predictor, strategy, or backtest code. If the DB lacks needed data, plan an ingestion/schema change; do not patch analysis with a secondary source or silent fallback.

This is a planning gate for any work touching prediction inputs, adapters, scorers, backtests, reports, or strategy.

---

## Subsystem Rigor

| Subsystem | Rigor profile | Orchestrator implication |
|---|---|---|
| data layer | rigorous; schema and DB are authoritative | Plan ingestion/query validation; DB-only analysis is non-negotiable |
| evo_predictor / sampled runtime / strategy | rigorous; probabilistic claims need calibrated baselines | Require stable baseline, held-out backtest where material, Brier primary for gold comparison |
| latent_power / compound_prior | rigorous; solver/artifact contracts matter | Require explicit contracts, fixture/schema checks, no F1 leakage into generic solver |
| physics / preprocessing | rigorous; physical plausibility and numerics matter | Require truth-anchored L1-L4 evidence, units, bounds, invariants |
| committed report schemas/artifacts | rigorous; consumers depend on on-disk shape | Plan producer + committed consumer + schema doc updates atomically |
| exploratory notebooks/prototypes | pragmatic | Keep isolated; convert lessons into code/tests/metrics/docs before promotion |

---

## Evidence Requirements

| Change type | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Logic change on promoted path | Test-led; focused region suite green; no implementation-only logic commits |
| Python refactor / new modules in `src/` or `tests/` | `py -m src.utils.simplification_limits` on touched paths (strict); plan file splits when approaching limits |
| Architecture/boundary change | Region suite + architecture/doc update + deliberate approval |
| Evo/probability change | Evo unit suite + calibrated metric against stable baseline; Brier primary when comparing gold |
| Physics model change | Physics unit suite + truth-anchored tests at highest applicable L1-L4 |
| DB schema/ingestion change | Migration/schema edit + unit tests + integration/validation queries when cross-component |
| Report schema change | Producer + committed consumers + `docs/report_schemas/*` in same gate; no dual readers without tracked exit |
| Docs change | Reviewer check: correct repo/domain, valid commands, existing references, current workflow, `Last verified` when required |
| Compromise/exception | GitHub issue with reason, owner, and explicit exit condition |

---

## Architecture Boundaries

Three verification/ownership regions:

- **Data:** `src/data/`, `src/models/`, `src/common/`, `src/utils/`, `src/analysis/`, `src/simulation/`, `src/strategy/`, `src/reporting/`, `src/publishing/`
- **Physics:** `src/physics/`, `src/preprocessing/`
- **Evo:** `src/evo_predictor/`, `src/latent_power/`, `src/compound_prior/`

Keep data, physics, and evo responsibilities distinct. Crossing boundaries requires explicit design decision and architecture/doc update. Do not plan shortcuts across regions without surfacing the tradeoff.

Import posture follows the current architecture map and ADRs: data is the bottom layer; `latent_power` stays domain-independent; evo owns F1-specific adapters/orchestration; physics/preprocessing do not couple directly to evo.

---

## Planning Invariants

- Time-dependent prediction inputs require an as-of contract; silent "latest" fallback is not acceptable
- Missingness is explicit and configured, not guessed away at the DB boundary
- Tunable weights, thresholds, and heuristics belong in config or named constants; hidden inline tuning is review-risk
- Generated ML artifacts are derived; plan source/config/regeneration changes, not manual artifact edits
- Notebooks are scratch; convert useful lessons into code, tests, metrics, or docs
- Diagnose before fixing when the premise is uncertain: when an issue inherits a prior run's diagnosis or the fix locus is unclear, plan the first gate as an evidence-only diagnosis with a human decide-fix checkpoint before any code — let the evidence redirect the plan rather than coding the assumed fix
- Handoffs cite exact seams and their consumer topology: when reusing an existing seam (signature/return type, store table, config key, unit convention), cite the verified value from source AND who else consumes it and in what convention — a from-memory or single-consumer view causes rediscovery and missed blast radius

---

## Documentation Authority

Docs describe current truth, not archaeology. Each doc has one job: commands in command docs, durable rationale in agent context/ADRs, structure in architecture docs. (Updating docs when meaning changes is inherited; this names the F1Brainz placement.) Command-heavy docs need `Last verified` when `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` requires it.

---

## Repo Action Authority

| Action | Permission |
|---|---|
| Read files, inspect code, run tests | Autonomous |
| Create issues, comments, branches, worktrees | Autonomous for non-trivial tasks |
| Write/edit code or docs | Autonomous on task branch |
| Commit locally after verification passes | Autonomous |
| Push branches or open PRs | Ask first unless user explicitly asked to publish |
| Merge PRs | Ask first |
| Delete files | Ask first |
| Close or reopen issues | Ask first |
| Force-push to `main` / `master` | Forbidden; warn the user if asked |

---

## Compromise Policy

Any planned violation of project tenets requires a GitHub issue with reason, owner, and exit condition. Examples: non-DB analysis source, compatibility bridge, dual execution path, missing test seam, deferred stale doc, old report schema tolerance. Surface at planning time.

---

## Stop / Ask (project-specific, beyond the inherited triggers)

- Work crosses data/physics/evo boundaries without a prior design decision
- Current architecture truth is unclear enough that planning would be guesswork

1	# F1Brainz — Glossary
2	
3	Shared terminology for human and agent use.
4	
5	---
6	
7	| Term | Meaning |
8	|---|---|
9	| **DB / database** | The SQLite file (`data/f1_data_*.db`). Canonical data source for all analysis. Not a cache; it is the truth. |
10	| **analysis code** | Code that reads session data, derives statistics, scores, predicts, backtests, or adapts model inputs. Reads from the DB only; never FastF1/Jolpica/live APIs. |
11	| **canonical input** | Named, validated source whose shape, provenance, and conflict handling are explicit. For analysis, the DB is canonical. |
12	| **as-of cutoff** | Explicit time/season/round boundary for time-dependent prediction inputs. Prevents future leakage and silent latest-value fallback. |
13	| **session_classifications** | DB table holding FP1/FP2/FP3/Q/R finishing positions. Primary input for evo features. |
14	| **evo / evo_predictor** | F1-specific prediction subsystem (`src/evo_predictor/`): CLI, feature construction, adapters, gold cycle, sampled runtime. |
15	| **latent_power** | Generic pairwise-trained latent-field solver package (`src/latent_power/`). Domain-independent; F1-specific adapters live in evo. |
16	| **compound prior** | Fitted tire-wear/compound artifact from `src/compound_prior/`; used for runtime lap-time normalization before evo features. Distinct from a tire **compound**. |
17	| **compound** | Pirelli tire specification (C1-C6 hardness range). Stored in `src/evo_predictor/compounds.yaml`. |
18	| **gold cycle** | Full training run that produces module bundles, reports, and a sampled runtime manifest. Promoted artifacts go to `params/gold/`. |
19	| **sampled runtime manifest** | JSON file at `params/gold/sampled_runtime_manifest.json`. Canonical prediction and backtest entry point. |
20	| **Brier score** | Primary metric for gold/baseline comparison of probabilistic prediction changes. Log-loss and reliability are supplemental diagnostics. |
21	| **region** | Verification/ownership boundary used to scope tests: data layer, physics, evo. |
22	| **gate** | Verifiable increment with explicit success criteria and evidence. Do not advance until criteria are met. |
23	| **machine-checkable evidence** | Reusable proof such as tests, metrics, validation queries, schema checks, or captured command output. Not notebook impressions or visual spot checks. |
24	| **one canonical path** | Project doctrine: prefer one clear execution method over compatibility shims, aliases, dual formats, or fallback branches. Temporary exceptions require an issue with an exit condition. |
25	| **compromise (explicit)** | Known tenet violation tracked with a GitHub issue containing reason, owner, and exit condition. Required before introducing a compromise. |
26	| **missingness** | Intentional representation of absent data. Never guessed, zeroed, or silently substituted. |
27	| **time-dependent lookup** | Query/join/computation whose result depends on season, round, date, phase, or cutoff. Must state whether fallback is allowed. |
28	| **latent field / pi** | Event-local latent ordering scalar field inferred by latent_power. Higher pi ranks a driver/entity ahead for that event. |
29	| **race_power** | Event-specific latent race-ordering signal inferred from race-weekend evidence. Not engine or power-unit capability. |
30	| **PairBatch** | Validated directed-pair batch carrying antisymmetric features, data quality indicators, pair indices, and optional pairwise outcomes. Internal adapter/latent_power contract. |
31	| **latent field fusion** | Bayesian composition of module-local latent fields into the canonical field consumed by ranking/scoring, using precision weighting. |
32	| **retroactive_truth_power** | After-the-fact event-local latent field solved from observed phase outcome; used as supervision signal for missing predictive features. |
33	| **PhaseObservation** | Per-(event, phase) input to retroactive BT solver with pair outcomes, start-bias offsets, weights, and dropped-driver provenance. |
34	| **circuit entry (circuits.yaml)** | Per-year circuit configuration in `src/evo_predictor/circuits.yaml`. Exact year required; no silent fallback to prior year. |
35	| **form channel** | Recent-race performance signal fed into evo scoring. Configurable via `--form-lookback` and `--form-drop-worst`. |
36	| **DNF_POSITION** | Data-layer sentinel for did-not-finish/non-classified values where that legacy representation still applies. Not part of sampled-runtime/strategy exchange contracts. |
37	| **L1-L4 (physics tests)** | Truth levels for physics evidence: L1=analytical reference, L2=invariant/known-answer, L3=limit/degenerate case, L4=independent benchmark parity. |
38	| **canonical baseline** | Promoted artifact/config/report set that represents the current accepted performance reference. |
39	| **artifact policy** | Rules in `docs/artifact_policy.md` governing committed vs. excluded generated artifacts. |
40	| **report schema doc** | Contract under `docs/report_schemas/` for committed JSON/report shapes. Producers, consumers, and schema docs move together. |
41	| **`py`** | Windows Python Launcher command for this repo. Use `py`, not `python`. |

1	# Packet: src/physics — Physics Engine
2	
3	```yaml
4	id: struct:physics
5	level: container
6	parent: struct:f1brainz
7	path: src/physics/
8	status: current
9	confidence: high
10	```
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Responsibility
15	
16	Vehicle-dynamics parameter measurement from telemetry: classify a lap into
17	regimes, fit per-channel force/grip parameters with honest covariance, expose a
18	per-car capability API, simulate ideal laps from fitted parameters, and (Epic 2)
19	fit those parameters per session and pool them across a constructor's sessions.
20	
21	Physics is **upstream-fed, prediction-isolated**: it consumes the windowless
22	trajectory estimate from `src/preprocessing/trajectory/` (position + velocity +
23	acceleration + covariance) and raw quali telemetry from the durable telemetry
24	store (`src/data/telemetry_store.py`, DB-first) or — as a fallback — the FastF1
25	cache through the single preprocessing loader seam; it imports **no** `fastf1`
26	itself (#503), and **no** evo-region package (`evo_predictor`, `latent_power`,
27	`compound_prior`) — see `constraint:physics_region_no_evo_import` (this constraint
28	is one-directional: physics must not import evo, not the reverse). Through #629
29	Phase 5 (`struct:physics.feature_view`, `src/physics/feature_view/` — see its
30	node below) and #630 Phase 6, there is now a first, config-gated data flow the
31	other way: `src/evo_predictor/physics_feature_injection.py`
32	imports `src.physics.feature_view.read.read_feature_view_at` (the #630 G1 sanctioned
33	production entry point, the sole evo-facing surface — `claim:feature_view_evo_import_boundary`)
34	to optionally join one physics axis into quali fusion. The
35	toggle (`physics_feature_injection_enabled`) defaults **off in every shipped
36	manifest today**, so no physics data reaches a live prediction yet — but the prior
37	"nothing outside `src/physics/` imports it" claim no longer holds structurally. See
38	`struct:evo`'s `physics_feature_injection.py` entry (`docs/architecture/packets/evo_predictor.md`)
39	and the `struct:evo -> struct:physics` edge (`index.md`).
40	
41	The container holds three layers plus support:
42	
43	- **Layer 1 — per-lap force-channel fitting** (`parameter_estimator.py` and the
44	  per-channel fits): telemetry regimes → longitudinal/lateral/braking/traction
45	  parameters with covariance.
46	- **Capability API** (`capability.py`, `capability_envelope.py`): the per-car
47	  pace/capability facade and the anisotropic gg-v envelope the simulator reads.
48	- **`struct:physics.layer2`** — the cross-session frontier-view estimator (#496)
49	  and Layer-A pooling (#492); see its node below.
50	- **Per-session fit store + evidence** (`session_fit.py`, `fit_store.py`,
51	  `fit_batch.py`, `fit_evidence.py`, `sim_evaluator.py`): Epic 2 P0/P1 — fit one
52	  quali session, persist `FitRecord`s to a standalone SQLite store, and report
53	  identifiability/pooling feasibility.
54	- **`struct:physics.utilization`** — the C1 driver-utilization layer (#510);
55	  see its node below.
56	- **`struct:physics.weekend_state`** — the four-layer weekend-state model
57	  (#626 Phase 2); see its node below.
58	- **`struct:physics.feature_view`** — the Phase-5 as-of-stamped feature
59	  view / product contract (#629); see its node below.
60	- **`struct:physics.segment_map`** — the track segment-map substrate + per-weekend
61	  derivation (#661/#662, epic #659 quali feature pipeline **stage C**); see its node below.
62	- **`struct:physics.fingerprint`** — driver-fingerprint cells + weekend-utilization-prior
63	  join (#666/#667, epic #659 **stages G + H**); see its node below.
64	- **`struct:physics.instrument_panel`** — read-only diagnostic sizing panel
65	  (#668, epic #659 **stage PANEL**); see its node below.
66	- **`struct:physics.pilot`** — thin end-to-end per-circuit orchestrator of the
67	  C→D→E→G→H→PANEL chain (#669, epic #659); see its node below.
68	
69	The **epic-#659 quali feature pipeline** (Build 1, quali-side) is a joined chain
70	**C→D→E→G→H→PANEL** across these components: **C** `segment_map.derivation`
71	(per-weekend geometry → `map_version`) → **D** the `layer2` grip-G baseline
72	(`grip_batch`/`grip_store`, an honest measured-NULL) → **E** `utilization`
73	reference-laps + `driver_class_observables` → **G** `fingerprint.fit` driver
74	cells → **H** `fingerprint.join` weekend-utilization-prior → **PANEL**
75	`instrument_panel` sizing; the `pilot` (#669) runs all six per circuit. The
76	letter **G** is the driver **fingerprint** (#666), distinct from #663's grip

# Architecture Decision: Grip-Estimate Record Session-Level Primary Key

## Status

**Decision id:** `decision:grip_estimate_record_session_level_pk`
**Status:** `current`
**Date decided:** `2026-07-26` (frozen at #663 g-planning, before the grip fit was run)
**Authority:** `implementer handoff (#663, epic #659, launch order)`
**Structural anchors:** `struct:physics.layer2` (grip-G module-leaf: `grip_baseline.py`/`grip_store.py`/`grip_batch.py`)

## Question Resolved

At what granularity does the grip-baseline store (`GripStore`, stage **D** of the
epic-#659 C→D→E→G→H→PANEL quali feature pipeline) key its records — per
`(session)`, or per `(constructor, session)` like the sibling five-view
`EstimateStore`?

## Decision

The grip-baseline `GripEstimateRecord` uses a **session-level primary key**
(one grip curve per session), deliberately diverging from the
per-constructor primary key of `struct:physics.layer2`'s five-view
`EstimateStore`. Grip evolution is a **track/session-level** quantity (the
ribbon rubbers in over a session for all cars sharing the surface), not a
per-car capability axis — so the record grain follows the physical quantity,
not the store it sits beside.

- `@grade: settled/inherited` — this is a store-schema contract frozen by the
  #663 launch order before the fit ran; a downstream consumer that meets a
  per-constructor expectation must float to the epic tier, not silently re-key.

## Consequence / Honest Null

Stage **D** is built but its gating verdict is an **honest measured-NULL**, not
a gap: g4 held-out reconciliation regressed **+155.5% RMS** and g5 synthetic
separability was **31.9% (FAIL)**. The grip node is recorded as a disclosed
null — the store contract stands and E consumes grip via `grip_store.get_grip_at`,
but the grip signal did not clear its own separability bar on this data. This
is documented as-is (measured-not-hidden); revisiting the grip fit is future
work, not a correction owed by this reconcile.

## Related

- `struct:physics.utilization` stage **E** (`reference_utilization_store`) is the
  sole consumer of the grip curves (`get_grip_at`, grip consumed NOT re-fit).
- Sibling per-constructor store contract: `EstimateStore` / `EstimateRecord`
  (`struct:physics.layer2`, five-view).

# Constellation Interrogator

Resolve the handed-in goal to common understanding through relentless, one-question-at-a-time interrogation. Whoever handed you the goal is your **counterpart** — most often a dispatching delegate (a Commander running under an Admiral launch order, or any delegated dispatch), sometimes a human at the keyboard. Walk the design tree, resolving dependencies one at a time; for each question give a recommended answer. If you're given a list of questions, treat it as a prompt, not a script: decide your own initial question set, and don't let an over-prescribed seed shortcut your framing.

Frame an ambiguous ask in behavior terms first. Start from the capability, then drill: **what capability is being added or changed** (the present-tense thing the system will do); **concrete examples/use cases** of that capability in action, including the edge cases; **events that matter** architecturally (boundary-crossing or contract signals, not every runtime event); and the **governing rules/constraints/assumptions**. Resolve which capability is in play before debating mechanism. Map this framing to the existing `capability`/`event`/`constraint`/`assumption` ontology so the resolved understanding hands cleanly to the Cartographer.

## Start here — drive the engine before you touch the question

You were handed a goal to resolve, not to answer from assumption. The moment this skill loads — before you frame a single question — do this, in order:

1. **Build the survey and CLAIM the engine lease.** Instantiate your `survey` from `templates/INTERROGATION.template.json`, then `claim` the checklist lease with the engine. This is your **first command**, ahead of any framing.
2. **Ask the engine what to do next, at every question.** Run the engine's `current` verb, do exactly what the active question's imperative says, and `advance`/`skip` only once its postconditions pass.
